Brief facts of the case
1.

In brief the case of the prosecution is that on 08.01.2000 at about 02.30 p.m, Food Inspector V. P.
S. Chaudhary along with FI D.V. Singh under the supervision and directions of SDM / LHA Sh. Arun Mishra visited M/s Gupta Brothers, 7340/1, Prem Nagar, Delhi07, where accused Subhash Gupta (accused no. 1 as per original complaint and since expired and proceedings against him were abated vide orders dated 29.09.2008) was found present conducting the business of various food articles including Mustard Oil ready for sale for human consumption which was contained in a sealed plastic bottle of half litre each and in compliance of the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the Act &
Rules) the Food Inspector collected / purchased the sample of Mustard Oil.
2.

During the course of investigation it was revealed that the sample commodity was supplied to Subhash Gupta by M/s Tika Ram Suresh Kumar of which accused Suresh Kumar (accused no. 2 as per original complaint and since expired and proceedings against him were abated vide orders dated 29.09.2008) was the proprietor and accused no. 1 Dinesh Kumar (accused no. 3 as per original complaint) was the person Incharge and responsible for the day to day conduct of the business of the said partnership firm.

3. It was further revealed accused Suresh Kumar had procured the sampled commodity from accused no. 2 i.e. M/s Raghubir Singh & Sons Oil and Flour Mills, Jhajjar, Haryana (accused no. 4 as per the original complaint) which was the manufacturing firm of which accused no. 3 Ram Avtar (accused no. 5 as per the original complaint) was the partnercumperson incharge and responsible for day to day conduct of the said firm.

It is further the prosecution's case that the sample was sent to Public Analyst for analysis and as per the report of Public Analyst the sample was found not conforming to the standards because saponification and iodine value exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 177 and 112 respectively.
Further
the sample also contained synthetic colouring matter.

5. After obtaining the necessary Sanction / Consent under Section 20 of the Act the present complaint was filed for violation of provisions of Section 2 (ia) (a) (j) &
(m) of PFA Act 1954 punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w Section 7 of the Act.
6. After the complaint was filed, the accused persons was summoned vide orders dated 11.09.2000.

Accused Subhash Gupta (deceased) after filing his appearance moved an application under Section 13(2) of PFA Act to get analyzed the second counterpart of the sample from Central Food Laboratory and consequent thereto second counterpart of the sample as per the choice of the accused was sent to Director, CFL (Calcutta) for its analysis vide orders dated 30.09.2000.

The Director so opined as the saponification and iodine value exceeded the prescribed maximum limit and sample also contained added colouring matter.

7. During the course of trial, accused Subhash Gupta (accused no. 1 as per original complaint) and accused Suresh Kumar (accused no. 2 as per original complaint) expired and proceedings against them were abated vide orders dated 29.09.2008 passed by Ld. Predecessor of this court.

8. In pre charge evidence, the prosecution examined one witness i.e. Food Inspector V.P.S.
Chaudhary as PW1 and pre charge evidence was closed vide orders dated 25.06.2009.

9. Charge for violation of provision of Section 2 (ia) (a) & (m) of PFA Act 1954 punishable U/s 16 (1)
(a) r/w section 7 of the Act were framed against accused persons vide orders dated 31.08.2009 to which accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
10.

Thereafter, in the post charge evidence the prosecution examined two witnesses i.e. FI V. P. S.
Chaudhary as PW1 and the then SDM/LHA Sh. Arun Mishra as PW2 and PE was closed vide orders dated 12.08.2010.
11. Statement of the accused persons U/s 313 Cr. P.C.
was recorded on 04.03.2011 wherein the accused persons claimed themselves to be innocent.
Despite opportunity given, accused persons failed to examine any witness in their defence.

A brief scrutiny of the evidence recorded in the matter is as under:
12. PW1 FI, Sh. V. P.S. Chaudhary deposed that on 08.01.2000 he alongwith FI D.
V. Singh under the supervision and direction of Sh. Arun Mishra, SDM/LHA went to M/s Gupta Brother, 7340/1, Prem Nagar, Delhi07, where accused Subhash Gupta (since expired) was found conducting the business of the food articles in the said shop including "Mustard Oil".
He deposed that he disclosed his identity and intention for taking the sample of mustard oil to which accused agreed.

He deposed that before taking the sample he tried his best to procure some public witnesses by requesting some neighbours, customers and passersby to join the sample proceedings but as none agreed, on his request FI D. V. Singh, agreed and joined as witness.
He deposed that at about 02.30 pm he purchased one sealed plastic bottle of half liter of mustard oil having label declaration on payment of Rs. 23/ vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW1/A.

He deposed that the plastic bottle was opened and the contents of the bottle i.e.
Mustard oil was divided into three equal parts by putting them in three clean and dry glass bottles.
He deposed that then each bottle containing the sample of Mustard Oil were separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
He deposed that LHA Slip bearing code number and signature of LHA was affixed on all the three counter parts of the bottle.

He deposed that then the vendor signatures were obtained on LHA Slip bearing his number and signature and the wrapper of the sample bottles in such a manner that a portion of his signature were on the wrapper as well as on the LHA Slip.
He deposed that the notice in Form VI Ex. PW1/B was Da vs . Subhash Gupta & Ors.

He deposed that Panchnama Ex.
PW1/C was prepared.
He deposed that vendor also disclosed that he purchased the sample bottle from Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar, Shop No. 921, Subji Mandi, Delhi07.
He deposed that accordingly, a Notice u/s 14A Ex. PW1/D was prepared at the spot and was sent through registered post on the next working day.

He deposed that all these documents Ex. PW1/A to Ex. PW1/D were read over and explained to the accused in Hindi and after understanding the same accused signed at point A, witness signed at point C and he signed at point B respectively.

He deposed that one counter part of the sample was deposited with the PA on 10.01.00 i.e on next day working day vide receipt Ex. PW1/E in a sealed packet containing one copy of memo in Form VII and another sealed envelop containing one copy of another memo in Form VII separately.

He deposed that the two counter parts of the sample alongwith two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited in intact condition with the LHA on 10.01.00 i.e next working day vide receipt Ex. PW1/F bearing his signature at point A with the intimation that one counter part of the sample has already been deposited in intact condition with the PA.
He deposed that all the copies of memo of Form VII bore the same seal impression with which the sample in question was sealed.
He deposed that the PA report Ex. PW1/G was received according to which, the sample was found not conforming to the standards, as mentioned therein at portion X.

He deposed that during investigation, he sent a letter Ex. PW1/H to STO, Ward No. 41 and reply received at portion A according to which, M/s Gupta Brothers was proprietorship firm and Sh. Subhash Chand (now expired) was the sole proprietor of its firm.

He deposed that he also sent a letter Ex. PW1/I to M/s Gupta Brothers and received his reply Ex.
PW1/I1 alongwith enclosures i.e. Copy of the sales tax and copy of MCD license.

He deposed that he also sent a letter Ex. PW1/J to Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar and received reply of their counsel Ex.
PW1/J1.

He deposed that he also sent a letter Ex. PW1/K to STO, Ward No. 40 and as per reply at portion A, M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar was proprietorship firm and Sh. Suresh Kumar was the sole proprietor of its firm.

He deposed that he also sent a letter Ex. PW1/L to M/s Raghubir & Sons,
Oil and Flour Mills, Jhajjar, Haryana and received the reply Ex. PW1/L1, according to which M/s Raghubir & Sons is a partnership firm having four partners and Sh. Ram Avtar was active partner and was incharge and responsible for day to day affairs of M/s Raghubir & Sons.
He deposed that he also received a letter Ex. PW1/J1 from one Dinesh Kumar that he is responsible for day to day affairs of M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar as Sh. Suresh Kumar was bed ridden.

He deposed that he also sent a letter Ex. PW1/I2 to vendor Subhash Gupta for production of the bill and account books, if any,
showing the purchase of the mustard oil and mode of payment and received their reply Ex. PW1/I3 alongwith copy of ledger and cash book Mark X & Y.

He deposed that he also sent a letter Ex.
PW1/L2 to M/s Raghubir Singh & Sons to provide the copy of the partnership deed and copy of license and received attested copy of registration certificate of small scale industries Mark 'Z' and also received reply Ex. PW1/M from Sh. R. S. Punia, Excise and Taxation Officer & Assessing Authority, Jhajjar, Haryana disclosing that M/s Raghubir Singh & Sons is a partnership firm having four partners and Sh. Ram Avtar was authorized to conduct and manage the business of the firm.

He deposed that then on the completion of the investigation, the complete case file along with all statutory documents were sent through LHA to the Director (PFA), Sh. Ashok Bakshi, who after going through the case file, applied his mind and gave his consent for prosecution Ex. PW1/N which Da vs . Subhash Gupta & Ors.

4 bears his signature at point A.

He deposed that the complaint Ex. PW1/O was filed in Court by him,
bearing his signature at point A.
He deposed that the intimation letter Ex. PW1/P alongwith the PA report was sent to accused by registered post by the SDM/LHA, which was not received back undelivered.

He deposed that the postal registration receipt copy is Ex. PW1/Q bearing the relevant entries at portion A & B.
13.
During the cross examination he admitted that vendor did not produce the bill in respect of purchase of sample commodity during investigation till today.
He stated that no record was seized of M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar after receiving the reply Ex. PW1/J1 through their counsel that they had not supplied the sample commodity to the vendor.
He denied the suggestion that he in connivance with the vendor falsely implicated M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar.
14. PW2 the then SDM/LHA Sh. Arun Mishra deposed on the same lines as deposed by PW1.
15. This so far is the prosecution evidence in the matter.
16. I have heard the arguments advanced at bar by the Ld. defence counsel as also the Ld. SPP for complainant.
I have also carefully gone through the evidence recorded in the matter and perused the documents placed on record by the prosecution in this case.
17. After hearing the rival contentions raised at Bar I am of the opinion that prosecution has miserably failed to bring home the guilt against accused persons.

18. The present prosecution was launched against accused no. 1 (accused no. 3 as per the original complaint) and Suresh Kumar (deceased and accused no. 2 as per the original complaint) on the basis of claim made by deceased accused/vendor Subhash Gupta (accused no. 1 as per the original complaint) at the time of lifting of the sample that he had purchased the sampled mustard oil bottles from M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar (accused no. 2 as per the original complaint, as it was a proprietorship concern of Suresh Kumar).
On the basis of claims made by Subhash Gupta the FI prepared notice u/s 14A i.e. Ex PW1/D addressing to Suresh Kumar (accused no. 2 as per the original complaint).

Suresh Kumar (accused no. 2 as per the original complaint) was impleaded as an accused in his capacity as the proprietor of the supplier firm and accused no. 1 Dinesh Kumar (accused no. 3 as per the original complaint) was impleaded in his capacity as the person incharge of and responsible for the conduct of day to day business of M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar.

As the sample of mustard oil was contained in sealed bottles of 500 Ml and the bottles as such were lifted for sampling i.e. in original sealed condition they were impleaded by the Food Inspector in their capacity as the supplier of the sampled commodity.

19. As far as accused no. 2 M/s Raghubir Singh & Sons Oil Flour Mills (accused no. 4 as per the original complaint) is concerned prosecution was launched against it on the basis of the label declaration as appearing on the sampled bottles as it was mentioned on the sample bottles as "quality product from M/s Raghubir Singh & Sons, Oil and Flour Mills, Jhajhar" i.e. in the capacity of manufacturer of the sampled product.

20. However the prosecution miserably failed to prove that the sampled commodity was supplied by M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar ( accused no. 2 as per the original complaint) to accused/deceased Subhash Gupta or that it was manufactured by M/s Raghubir Singh & Sons, Oil and Flour Mills,
Jhajjar (accused no. 5 as per original complaint) and supplied by it to M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar who in turn supplied it to deceased/accused/vendor Subhash Gupta.
21. Accused/vendor Subhash Gupta did not submit any bill to the Food Inspector to corroborate/
substantiate his claim that the sampled commodity was supplied to him by accused/deceased Suresh Kumar i.e. accused no. 2 as per the original complaint and accused no. 1 (accused no. 3 as per the original complaint).

sentences.text: The Food Inspector admitted during his cross examination that till date neither the original bill nor the photocopy of the same was supplied to him by accused Subhash Gupta.

Subhash Gupta instead of supplying the bill to corroborate his claims had replied to the Food Inspector regarding his queries vide Ex PW1/I1 dated 02.03.2000 wherein he claimed that the photocopy of the bill vide which he had purchased the sampled commodity from M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar has been misplaced and he is unable to submit the same.
He further claimed that despite repeated requests Dinesh Kumar (accused no. 1) who sits at M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar has not been supplying the duplicate bill despite repeated requests.
This letter was followed by another letter/communication dated 06.05.2000 wherein he claimed that Dinesh Kumar had categorically told him that he would not supply any duplicate bill.
Hence Subhash Gupta could only make bald claims regarding supply of the sampled commodity to him by accused Suresh Kumar/M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar and accused no. 1.

In the absence of any bill, invoice, receipt etc. no benefit of warranty could be granted to accused Subhash Gupta and accordingly no liability could be fastened upon either M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar or Dinesh Kumar when they categorically denied vide Ex. PW1/J1 the supply or sale of the sampled commodity to Subhash Gupta.

22. In order to seek the benefit of Section 19(2) r/w Section 14 of the Act, the vendor was obliged to prove that he had purchased the article of food in question from a manufacturer / distributor or dealer with a written warranty in the prescribed form and that the article of food so purchased was properly stored while it was in his possession and he sold it in the same state as it was purchased by him.
Proviso of Section 14 creates a fiction that a bill, cash memo or invoice given by distributor or dealer to the vendor shall be deemed to be a warranty.

Hence, even if the vendor is unable to produce a warranty in Form VIA, the bill or cash memo given to him by the manufacturer or distributor will be enough to satisfy the requirements of sub section (2) of Section 19 of the Act.

Reliance may be placed upon AIR 1960 SC 12 and AIR 1984 SC 192.
23.

In Pothuri Ananda Venkta Shubha Rao Gupta Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh 1991 FAC 79, it was held that the burden is on the accused to produce the warranty and prove that he purchased the food article under warranty from a particular person.

sentences.text: Mere filing of the photocopy of the bill / the warranty without filing the original in the court will not be of any help of the accused / the vendor.

Further reliance may be placed upon the law laid down in Raja Das G. Pemnani Vs. State of Maharashtra AIR 1975 SC 189, A. Ghosh Vs. State of Rajasthan 2006 FAJ 229, Sham Sunder Da vs . Subhash Gupta & Ors.

Hence, not only the accused has to prove that he has purchased the article from a particular manufacturer / distributor but further that the article was sold by him in the same manner / state /
condition as it was purchased by him.
Unless there is material to show that he was selling in the same state in which it was purchased, the petitioner can not get benefit of Section 19(2) of the Act.

Reliance may be placed upon law laid down in H.A. Rasheed Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh 1996 (1)
FAC 78, Inderjit Vs. State of Haryana FAJ 370, Swapan Kumar Vs. Anil Kumar 1988 CrLJ 60, 1981 (1) FAC 275, and Apurba Poddar Vs. State of Assam 2006 (1) FAC 22 25.

sentences.text: The ledger i.e. Mark X and Y which the accused/vendor/ deceased Subhash Gupta annexed with his reply Ex. PW1/I3 is insufficient document to prove the factum of supply/sale of sampled commodity to him.

It is a document belonging to the deceased/accused and in the absence of any other supporting material/evidence in the form of bill, invoice etc. or the testimony of a person in whose presence the sale was effected or who was instrumental in effecting the sale or being a witness to the document whereby the sale transaction was completed no benefit of warranty can be given to accused Subhash Gupta or the corresponding liability fix upon accused no. 1.
26.

As far accused no. 2 and 3 are concerned (accused no. 4 and 5 as per the original complaint) they were prosecuted by the Food Inspector being the manufacturing unit and the Incharge of the manufacturing unit respectively.
As far as accused no. 2 is concerned the Food Inspector prosecuted it solely on the basis of the label declaration as appearing on the sampled bottles.

Apart from the label declaration the Food Inspector did not collect any document during the course of investigation nor could anything be proved on record to the effect that sampled commodity was indeed manufactured by accused no. 2.
They had denied vide Ex. PW1/L1 the supplying of sampled commodity either to M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar or to Subhash Gupta directly.

In fact accused Suresh Kumar/M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar and accused no. 1 Dinesh Kumar (accused no. 3 as per the original complaint) nowhere claimed that they had themselves procured the sampled commodity from accused no. 2 and 3 (accused no. 4 and 5 as per the original complaint).

As already discussed above accused Suresh Kumar and M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar had denied supplying or sale of sampled commodity to Subhash Gupta and accordingly they did not claim that they themselves were supplied the sampled commodity by accused no. 2 and 3.

There is no invoice,
receipt, bill etc. which the Food Inspector could place/prove on record to show that the sampled commodity was either manufactured by accused no. 2 and 3 or supplied by accused no. 2 and 3 to accused no. 1 and M/s Teeka Ram Suresh Kumar or directly to Subhash Gupta.
Not only there is no proof of supply but also there is no proof that they were the manufacturer of the sampled commodity.

In these circumstances, there shall always be a doubt regarding the genuineness of the product sold by accused Subhash Gupta to the Food Inspector that is to say that it was manufactured by accused no. 2 and 3 as there are numerous spurious/duplicate products being sold in the market using the brand name of the original product.
The chain of supply or the factum of manufacturing could not be proved either by the prosecution or by the deceased Subhash Gupta.
Da vs . Subhash Gupta & Ors.

Page 1 Of 15 on 21 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92574508/
7 27.
Accordingly, accused no. 1 to 3 are entitled to acquittal as the sampled product could not be connected to them.

Maheshwari Vs. State of Assam 2006 (1) FAC 14, Apurba Poddar Vs. State of Assam 2006 (1) FAC 22 and State of Gujarat Vs. M/s Ashok Kumar Sheetal Das Firm 2006 (1) FAC 1.
24.
Hence, not only the accused has to prove that he has purchased the article from a particular manufacturer / distributor but further that the article was sold by him in the same manner / state /
condition as it was purchased by him.
Unless there is material to show that he was selling in the same state in which it was purchased, the petitioner can not get benefit of Section 19(2) of the Act.
Reliance may be placed upon law laid down in H.A. Rasheed Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh 1996 (1)
FAC 78, Inderjit Vs. State of Haryana FAJ 370, Swapan Kumar Vs. Anil Kumar 1988 CrLJ 60, 1981 (1) FAC 275, and Apurba Poddar Vs. State of Assam 2006 (1) FAC 22 25.
It is a document belonging to the deceased/accused and in the absence of any other supporting material/evidence in the form of bill, invoice etc. or the testimony of a person in whose presence the sale was effected or who was instrumental in effecting the sale or being a witness to the document whereby the sale transaction was completed no benefit of warranty can be given to accused Subhash Gupta or the corresponding liability fix upon accused no. 1.
26.
Not only there is no proof of supply but also there is no proof that they were the manufacturer of the sampled commodity.
In these circumstances, there shall always be a doubt regarding the genuineness of the product sold by accused Subhash Gupta to the Food Inspector that is to say that it was manufactured by accused no. 2 and 3 as there are numerous spurious/duplicate products being sold in the market using the brand name of the original product.
The chain of supply or the factum of manufacturing could not be proved either by the prosecution or by the deceased Subhash Gupta.
opennyai_summary.decision: Accordingly, accused no. 1 to 3 are entitled to acquittal as the sampled product could not be connected to them.
